title: Brass and Pressure: Steampunk Combat Sound Effects
shortText: 129 steampunk combat SFX: steam and air guns, gadgets, clockwork foes that wind down, brass UI. WAV + OGG.
html:
A steampunk battle, as one sound

129 sound effects for steampunk combat: five steam and air guns in every state, six gadget weapons, three clockwork foes that wind down as they lose health, brass armour, a battle interface and four battle beds, in one brass, iron and steam sound.

Licence, up front

Royalty free. Commercial use. No attribution required. Use it in as many games as you like, on any platform. The one thing you may not do is resell or redistribute the sounds themselves as a sound pack. The plain language terms ship as LICENSE.txt, with a copy and paste credit line for anyone who wants one. Everything is synthesised from code, so there is no upstream sample licence behind it.

Hear it first

There is a free demo on this page: 28 sounds copied unaltered from the paid files. The steam pistol in every state, the brass soldier winding down through all five rungs and in every state, the gear saw in every state, five battle interface cues and the boiler room.

Five guns, every state

No powder anywhere: every gun is driven by steam or by compressed air, so a shot is a valve snapping open, a burst of released pressure, the barrel ringing and the steam it leaves behind. Each gun ships fire, charge, vent, dry fire and jam.

  • Steam pistol: a brass sidearm fed by a small boiler cell: a hand pump to charge it, a sharp valve shot.
  • Pneumatic rifle: a long air rifle charged by a lever pump and a ratchet, a hard crack of released air.
  • Scatter gun: a short barrelled steam gun that throws a spray of shot, charged with one long slide.
  • Harpoon gun: a spring and air harpoon whose line pays out after the shot, charged by a winch crank.
  • Hand boiler cannon: a shoulder cannon with its own firebox: the boiler builds pressure, the shot is a deep iron blast.

Checked from the shipped files, not promised: across the gun by state grid the gun changes the sound and so does the state (100 pairs, 0 alike). Wiring it is one string: steam_pistol_vent, boiler_cannon_jam.

Foes that wind down as they lose health

Three clockwork foes, three sizes. Each one has a wind down ladder: five seamless loops of exactly 8 ticks, each beat 1.3x slower than the last, so a foe can sound more spent as its health falls. Wire the rung to its remaining health and swap the loop.

  • Tinker mite: a palm sized clockwork mite: a fast cog chatter that slows as it runs down; its beat runs from 0.125 s a tick at full health to 0.357 s nearly spent.
  • Brass soldier: a man sized brass automaton: a tick and a tock that stretch apart as its spring loses tension; its beat runs from 0.250 s a tick at full health to 0.714 s nearly spent.
  • Steam juggernaut: an iron giant with a firebox: a heavy anchor tick and a steam chuff on every beat, slowing to a crawl; its beat runs from 0.400 s a tick at full health to 1.142 s nearly spent.

Each foe also alerts, telegraphs a blow (a spring winding), strikes, takes hits, walks and dies (a spring snapping, gears spilling). Measured from the shipped files: 20 ladder steps across the pack, failing steps: 0.

Gadget weapons, whole lifecycles

A gear saw that spins up, runs as a loop, bites and coasts down; a spring blade out, in and slashing; a pressure hammer that charges, strikes and vents; a clockwork grenade you wind, hear ticking as a loop and lose; a galvanic coil that charges, discharges and fizzles; and a grapple that fires, catches, reels in as a loop and lets go. No two states of one gadget or foe are the same sound renamed (54 pairs measured, 0 alike).

The rest of the fight

  • 15 armour and impact sounds: one brass plate struck at five forces for damage tiers, rivets popping, shield blocks, a dent, a gauge shattering, a pipe bursting, cogs spilling across the floor and a steam leak loop.
  • 17 battle interface sounds: turn start, skill select, cursor takes, confirm, cancel, target lock, item use, a critical, an overheat warning loop, a pressure gauge that clicks into five notches, victory as one steam whistle and a valve, and defeat as a mainspring running down.
  • 4 battle beds, as loops: a boiler room, a foundry floor, the inside of a clock tower and rooftop pipes in the rain.

Fit

  • WAV and OGG for every file, 16 bit, 44.1 kHz, mono, with a naming manifest listing every file by group.
  • 24 seamless loops with loop points in both formats, and none on a one shot.
  • One hall: every one shot sits in the same iron hall, so the pack sounds like one place. The interface is dry.
  • 15 variation sets whose takes differ in length and in brightness.
  • One loudness band: the inner 80 percent of the pack sits inside 1.61 dB, so a boiler cannon and a menu cursor share a mix.
  • Import notes for Unity, Unreal, Godot, GameMaker, RPG Maker and the web, and pack_proof.json with a sha256 and a measurement for every file: 1196 checks, 0 failed.

Already own our other sound packs?

Every file here was measured against every file in the studio's 5 nearest packs (the clockwork world, black powder guns, electric robots, the steam railway and medieval impacts: 79077 pairs, on spectral shape and on envelope, each tolerant of a transposition): 79077 of 79077 are separate sounds. The proof ships in the download as cross_pack_proof.json.

Honest limits

These are synthesised sounds designed for games, not field recordings: brass valves, plates and gears, cast iron, steel springs, glass gauges and steam. The guns are pressure guns, not firearm recordings. The figures above are signal measurements, not a claim that anything sounds good; that is what the free demo is for. There are no voices and no music: the foes are machines, and victory is a single steam whistle, never a jingle.

AI disclosure, stated truthfully: the code that generates these sounds was written with AI assistance. The sounds themselves are self contained procedural synthesis by Core Systems Asset Factory, with no generative audio model at any point. The cover is an AI generated illustration, and the store plates are drawn by AI written code from the pack's own waveforms.

More from the same studio

  • Escapement, the steampunk world this fight happens in: clockwork, gears, springs, steam, levers, chimes and machine room loops.
  • Iron Road, the steam railway: locomotives, carriages, stations and signals.
  • Servo, electric robots and mechs, for the other kind of machine enemy.
  • Sixgun, the western frontier, with its black powder guns.
